# Agent sessions — naming, dispatch, verification, archival

Normative. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first.

A *Codex session* is one `codex exec` run: a single model conversation with a
working root, a sandbox mode, a persona, a task, and a token bill. In the
parent repository a session was a GitHub Actions job — its identity came from
a bot token, its prompt from a trusted checkout of the default branch, and its
accounting from the Actions API (`.github/workflows/claude.yml`,
`pr-review.yml`, `auto-fix.yml`). None of those three services exist locally,
so this protocol reconstructs each one explicitly:

| GitHub-era service | Local reconstruction |
|---|---|
| bot identity (`BOT_PAT`, `claude[bot]`) | the session name and `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` |
| trusted prompt checkout (`.trusted-actions/`, default branch) | `git show main:<persona>` inside `dispatch.sh` |
| run accounting (Actions API, run ids, job logs) | the captured `--json` event stream + `telemetry.py` |
| `@claude` / `@codex` mention trigger with an `author_association` gate | the human or orchestrator who runs `dispatch.sh` |
| Codex-cloud environment hooks (`.codex/setup.sh`, `.codex/maintenance.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`, run before dispatch |
| agent-runtime "pinned memories" (`AGENTS.md:658`) | the registry plus the archived capture files |

## 1. One entry point

**Every external Codex session is started by `local/bin/dispatch.sh`.** Calling `codex` by
hand — including from inside an agent session — is a protocol violation, not a
shortcut: the thread id, the token counts and the wall time exist only in the
event stream that `dispatch.sh` captures, and a session started any other way
is invisible to the study. `meta.md` permits exactly one repair: backfill a
registry line with `dispatcher: manual`, and log why in
`results/telemetry/events.md`.

This rule is inherited, not invented. The parent repository refused to start
an agent from an untrusted trigger for the same structural reason — a runner
with write permissions and secrets must have a single, gated entry
(`claude.yml:24-30`: "this workflow runs with write permissions and repo
secrets, so prompt-injection from untrusted commenters must not start the
runner"). Locally the secrets are gone but the write access is not.

An agent that needs a sub-session (an orchestrator splitting work, a prover
asking for a scout) invokes `dispatch.sh` from inside its own session, with
`MIPSTARRE_SESSION` set to its own name so the registry records the parent in
the `dispatcher` field. External session prompts prohibit further fan-out.

### Retired native descendants (historical amendments, 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-08)

Issue #505 retires the lease-based native entrypoints below and the useful-queue
supervisor. This subsection records historical episodes, not current admission
instructions. Native telemetry remains readable; new work uses external dispatch.

Main may assign useful native work under the published model policy without
external admission. Main remains Astra Ultra; existing defaults may stay Astra
during transition, while reviewed future defaults and explicit child choices use Sol. Before
admitting either kind of worker, reserve the native root's configured descendant cap:
`account_router.py native-lease CACHE ROOT_THREAD PID CAP`. The cap excludes the root;
the process census separately charges the root. This command validates the live
resume thread, process start identity, scoped space route, explicit Astra/Ultra
main configuration, policy-authorized child default and unchanged shared cap. Python 3.10 needs
`tomli` for this native-only TOML validation; Python 3.11 has `tomllib`.
`watchdog/primary-key-capacity` is the owner allocation, not measured throughput. For
the current Space episode the owner allocation is ten total sessions: the root plus at
most nine native descendants. The useful target is nine descendants, the floor is eight,
and external admission is zero. This supersedes the historical five-session episode; it
does not resize a live lease or create another pool. The
router enforces `watchdog/primary-external-admission=0` (and the owner `max-codex=0`
fallback) before creating any external reservation.
Native leases, external processes/reservations, interactives and reserved non-Codex
use all consume it. Unknown/dead native leases are retained until explicit
`native-lease ... --release` verifies the original root is no longer alive. A live
lease cannot be resized; checkpoint and refresh the process with owner coordination.

Main owns task selection, one-writer worktree assignments and native replenishment.
While slots are occupied, main and the central integration coordinator keep useful,
disjoint successors prepared against expected completions. A prepared record binds the
issue, worktree or read-only scope, exact current head or source snapshot, actually
published inputs, an eligible native identity and role, current worktree or unique
CI/review/publisher ownership, predecessor, job class, exact model and effort, a complete
hash-bound dispatch body, deadline rule, completion condition, cumulative budget,
authorized time limit, and any inherited deadline. Record `ready_at` when all checks finish
while the predecessor still occupies its slot. A prose description of expected inputs or
one nominal successor line is not ready. A head, dependency, ownership, role, or deadline
change invalidates readiness.
Each expected completion has a separately validated alternate; if none exists, record the
exact frontier blocker and do not call that completion fully prepared.

An ordinary proof or CI-handoff record may retain the complete body in either the existing
literal activation message or an immutable full contract. The contract form records an
absolute `contract_path`, the SHA-256 of its exact bytes, and the exact short activation
message sealed before predecessor completion. The full contract still contains every field
above, including preserved costs and a budget rule anchored to actual native `task_started`;
the short message contains only actor, operation id, contract path and hash, and a
conservative absolute deadline. The #471 brief fixes the schema and example. Existing full
messages remain valid.

On an attributable `task_complete` or equivalent terminal event, the coordinator first
rechecks only shared-cap admission, target identity, prepared-record immutability, owned
operation or worktree, and the remaining source budget. The activation payload carries
an absolute source deadline no later than the native call time plus the authorized limit;
a continuation retains an earlier inherited deadline. It then calls native `followup_task`
or `spawn_agent` before detailed predecessor receipt adoption, rollout tail reads,
capture hashing, broad censuses, or PR-history inspection. If the first prepared successor
is blocked or its activation call fails, record the exact prerequisite or failure and try
the prepared alternate in the same completion cycle. A quiet live turn remains occupied
until assignment, budget, and owned-operation checks establish an actual completion or
stall; silence alone does not create a vacancy.

For a contract-form ordinary record, the activator also verifies the full-contract hash,
the exact presealed short message, and every admission prerequisite that could have changed
before making the native call. It sends that short message without regenerating the full
arguments. A missing, unreadable, or mismatched contract or message invalidates the
candidate and selects another prepared useful alternative. No additional root round trip
is required for this already-authorized ordinary mechanical activation.

Canonical review consumption is a required admission blocker, not detailed receipt
adoption. A completed native reviewer thread remains idle and unavailable for follow-up
until `native_review.py complete` has validated its genuine result and created the bound
response, and the waiting canonical consumer has accepted that response. A response file
alone is not consumer acceptance. The held reviewer is not useful activity or an occupied
runtime slot; fill available capacity with another eligible prepared actor or job rather
than resuming it before the hold is released.

After the activation call, reconcile the fixed deadline against the successor's actual
current `task_started`, then verify its thread and turn, requested and observed model and
effort, and first useful output. Time before the first tool or progress report counts;
neither event starts a fresh budget. The coordinator owns an append-only transition batch
containing predecessor completion, `ready_at`, the actual activation call, successor start
and first output, the absolute source deadline, and real blocker intervals. Only after that
activation does detailed predecessor adoption proceed.
For a contract-form ordinary task, the actor verifies the same hash and reads the full
contract before any mutation. It rechecks its identity, model and effort, exact scope and
ownership, current inputs, and deadline. The effective deadline is the earliest of the
presealed absolute deadline, actual `task_started` plus the authorized duration, and any
inherited deadline; no first-tool or progress event resets it.
Waiting for successor start evidence or adopting one predecessor never serializes the
activation-first handling of another real completion.
An initial recovery of an old vacancy is labelled backlog, and one closing eight- or
nine-worker snapshot is not evidence of a prompt reaction or sustained coverage. Count
occupied runtime, fresh-output lower bounds, API usage, and proof delivery separately;
unknown is not zero and a ready list is not occupancy. No nested extra pool may exceed
the shared cap.
Operational acceptance requires a natural post-merge completion whose coordinator-owned
batch shows `ready_at` before completion, the actual activation call before detailed
adoption, and the successor's current `task_started` and first useful output. That one
transition establishes ordering, not sustained floor coverage; the existing interval audit
remains the latter's evidence.
Children do not write the primary index or shared telemetry concurrently. The primary
telemetry owner records each child using `telemetry.py native-record ROLLOUT` with
`--name --role --issue --thread-id --root-thread-id --key-label --worktree --status`
and `--job-class --requested-model`, plus `--hardness-reason` for hard Astra jobs.
Effective bound-turn contexts must satisfy the recorded classification. Root/parent IDs,
timestamps, outcome and raw observed counters are retained. Aggregation scope is
unknown: never sum parent and child counters without independent evidence. Native
review uses the exact-head transport in `review.md`; it cannot bypass CI or merge gates.
Canonical review assignments never use the ordinary short-contract form. Their literal
nonce, head, prompt digest and root assignment, direct-parent and independence checks, and
consumer identity holds remain in the activation message and review transport unchanged.
The root's inherited permission envelope is unchanged; reviewers receive read-only
assignments, not a falsely claimed separate read-only sandbox. Historical episodes,
attempt counts and usage survive refreshes and route changes without a budget reset.

## 2. Roles and sandboxes

### Sol-first jobs (superseding owner amendment, 2026-09-07)

Issue #301 comment5573256033 supersedes the earlier cleanup-only whitelist.
Routine/bounded jobs default to exact `gpt-5.6-sol`/`ultra`, including routine
existing-statement proof work, build repairs and independent reviews. Main chooses
`--job-class hard|escalated|source_semantic|control_policy|hard_review` with an
explicit `--hardness-reason` for genuinely difficult or escalated Astra work.
New game/hypothesis/source-semantic decisions and control-policy reviews justify
Astra; Lean files, prover/reviewer roles, or missing historical samples alone do not.
Exact edit specifications remain appropriate for mechanical cleanup, not a universal
Sol gate. The historical C01/C02 audit is retained as evidence, not a role ceiling.

For a model change, create a new explicit-model external assignment with Ultra;
`dispatch.sh --resume` does not switch an existing thread's model. Link the
predecessor thread, assignment, worktree, checkpoint and cumulative budget.
Observed models are not inferred from a requested argument. Independent review
still binds a different session to the exact head and trusted prompt. Hard
control-policy review remains Astra.

At reviewed activation, main records one timestamp in
`MIPSTARRE_MODEL_POLICY_ACTIVATION_AT`. External dispatch records `new` or
`resume` automatically; historical pre-activation native tasks remain
`grandfathered`. Grandfathering requires actual pre-activation turn evidence,
not a caller label. Main is excluded.
`model_policy.py --ratio-registry results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl --activation-at
TIMESTAMP` reports the last 100 distinct new dispatches, plus separate cumulative
counts. Target 20:1 within 10:1..50:1; unknown observations are not invented,
later known observations resolve them, and contradictory observations stay unknown.
Zero Astra is not a measurable ratio. Record finite-prefix/availability deviations;
never add filler or delay necessary hard work to manufacture a ratio.

No live activation until normal CI, independent control-policy review, service
merge and an explicit new Sol/Ultra runtime observation. Catalog/CLI Ultra is not
provider-measured reasoning. External admission uses the worker caps in section 4.
Deploy the shim with its adjacent checked helper, never as a stale standalone
copy. Keep all normal
caller, declaration, statement-integrity, proof-debt, CI/review and merge gates.
Escalation preserves all accumulated attempts, time, work and historical evidence.

Eight roles, fixed (`DESIGN.md`, "Naming and identity conventions"):

`orc`, `prover`, `reviewer`, `simplifier`, `blueprint`, `splitter`, `scout`,
`mathfix`.

Sandbox defaults follow from what the role is allowed to change:

| Role | Default sandbox | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `reviewer`, `scout` | `read-only` | a reader must not be able to edit what it reports on |
| all others | `workspace-write` | they exist to change the worktree |

`--sandbox` overrides the default; asking for a writable reviewer produces a
loud warning, because a reviewer that can fix what it found has reviewed its
own diff (§6). `danger-full-access` disables the codex sandbox entirely and
warns; it is never a default.

The persona for a role lives at `local/personas/<role>.md`, with one naming
exception: the role code `orc` maps to `local/personas/orchestrator.md`.
Until such a file is committed, `dispatch.sh` warns and falls back to a
one-line built-in frame — enough to run, not enough for load-bearing work.
The `mathfix` role is the source-statement repair lane governed by
`issues-prs.md` section 6: main selects Astra Ultra after the #26 availability report,
supplying cumulative per-gap budgets; historical Fable records remain in `owner-sessions.jsonl`.

## 3. Naming

```
<role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>        e.g. prover-0042-20260830-01
```

- `scope` is the `--issue` argument normalized to `[a-z0-9-]`, at most 40
  characters. An argument containing any of `[ ] ~ ^ : ? * \` is **rejected**,
  not sanitized. This is the bracket-free naming invariant
  (`DESIGN.md` invariant 9): the parent repository traced a class of automation
  failures to `]` surviving from bracketed issue titles into generated branch
  names, and adopted the convention as the fix
  (`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
  Rejecting rather than stripping keeps the session name, the branch name and
  the issue id referring to the same string.
- `seq` is a two-digit counter, allocated under
  `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/session-seq.lock` by scanning *both*
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` and `results/telemetry/sessions/` — a
  session that crashed before its registry line was written still owns its
  number, because its capture file exists.
- Names are stable identifiers: they appear in the registry, in capture file
  names, in the `dispatcher` field of child sessions, and in `audits/` reports.
  Never reuse one.

## 4. Lifecycle

### 4.1 Dispatch

```bash
local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover --issue 0042 \
  --worktree .worktrees/issue-0042-pauli-basis \
  --effort ultra \
  -- "Close the sorry at MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean:212 ..."
```

`dispatch.sh` performs, in order: role and scope validation; kill-switch check
(§9); session-name allocation; git-hook installation and verification in the
worktree; persona read from the trusted ref; prompt composition; the codex run
with the event stream teed to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`;
registry append; and a final report of `name`, `thread_id` and the
last-message path.

Account routing uses `--account auto|primary|second`, overriding
`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_ACCOUNT` (default `auto`). `account_router.py reserve ROOT ACCOUNT PID WAIT`
prints the selected account. Under `accounts/router.lock`, it reads only
`watchdog/max-codex-{primary,second}`: missing means zero, zero disables an
account, and negative or malformed caps fail. Live `accounts/<account>/<pid>`
marker files consume slots; dead markers are removed and permission-denied PIDs
remain occupied. Auto chooses the smallest live/cap ratio among accounts with
space, with primary winning ties. Explicit accounts never spill to the other.
Full accounts poll every 10 seconds for at most `MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNT_WAIT` seconds
(default 1800), rereading caps each time. Dry runs neither wait nor reserve.
No host census, global cap, account-mode, external-admission, native lease or
queue ticket participates. Configure worker caps to reflect the operator's allocation;
this command does not measure provider throughput or account for unmarked processes.
The installed `qpbt-switch` must be retired or made report-only by the meta session;
never run it to stop dispatchers, create HOLD/STOP files, or signal routers.
The repository change does not alter installed home commands or live caps.
Dispatch also supplies its registry to retain model selection and telemetry.
Resume affinity comes from registry account fields or rollout files in either
home; unknown, ambiguous, or conflicting selections fail before execution.
Resumes remain on their original account and model and obey that account's worker cap.
`--continue-from FILE` starts a fresh primary thread from operator JSON: `previous_session`
(terminal, same issue), `checkpoint` (ancestor of HEAD), and `budget_file` (shared path).
The budget contains `anchor`, `attempt_limit`, `attempts`, `working_seconds`, and
`sessions` (charged names including the predecessor); an unused attempt is required.
Continuations retain path, anchor and limit; monotone charges include snapshot plus completed
segments. Rows link original account/thread, checkpoint and budget. Operators enforce budgets;
route switches grant no reset/attempt or change to old homes, captures or uncommitted work.
Ordinary resumes recover prior provenance,
skipping malformed/non-object history rows but rejecting invalid relevant metadata.
Replay reads the private launch-time `.continuation.json`, never a later budget file.
The shim rejects multi-agent enable flags and whole `features`/`agents` overrides only.
Primary unsets inherited `CODEX_HOME`; second sets it for execution and rollout
lookup to `MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND` (default
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy`). Review and autofix inherit these
variables unchanged. The published owner policy selects exact Sol for routine jobs
and Astra for hard jobs with a reason; mathfix remains a hard role. Resumes do not
switch model or reset budgets. Dispatch `--effort`, `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT` and
`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_EFFORT` default to `ultra`; every other effort fails rather than
being normalized. The owner's verified space login is not rewritten here; the
historical scoped-home directory name may still contain `relay1` for continuity.
`requested_effort` is configured, not verified; see `meta.md`. Missing dispatchers fail closed.

Preconditions the dispatcher (human or orchestrator) owns:

1. The worktree exists and has been prepared by `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`.
   `dispatch.sh` creates no worktrees and fetches no caches; it fails with a
   message naming the setup script.
2. The git hooks are installed there. `dispatch.sh` installs and verifies them
   for every writing session, because `core.hooksPath` is per-worktree and a
   fresh worktree starts unprotected. Locally there is no CI backstop, so the
   hooks are the only gate that catches statement drift before it is committed
   (`AGENTS.md:83-85`).
3. The task prompt is self-contained. A dispatched session cannot see the
   dispatcher's conversation; write to it as to a colleague who was not in the
   room, citing files, blueprint labels and theorem names rather than "the
   thing we discussed".

Data the session should read but not obey — build logs, review findings, issue
bodies — is attached with `--context-file`, never pasted into the task text
(§7).

### 4.2 Work

The session works in its worktree under its sandbox. The standing rules
injected into every prompt are: read `AGENTS.md` first; treat
`local/protocols/*.md` as normative; start no sub-session except through
external `dispatch.sh`; never review your own diff;
keep runtime state out of the
repository; and put the result, the residual risk and the hand-off in the
final message, which is captured to
`results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.last.md`.

### 4.3 Verify

A session is not finished when the model stops. Before its work is accepted:

1. the validation ladder from `AGENTS.md` has been run (single-file
   `lake env lean` checks, then the `sorry`/`axiom` scan, then `lake build`);
2. the hooks pass — a failing `pre-push` is the local equivalent of a red CI
   and keeps the branch unmerged;
3. for Lean or blueprint changes, a **different** session has reviewed the
   diff (§6);
4. the final message exists and says what was done, what was not, and what the
   next session needs. An empty `<name>.last.md` is reported as a warning by
   `dispatch.sh` and should be treated as an incomplete session.

Verification failures are not silent. A failed codex run is recorded with
`status: failed` and its exit code, and `dispatch.sh` exits with that code —
the same fail-loudly semantics the parent repository adopted after a skipped
review read as green (`pr-review.yml:59-60`: "PR Review must not report
success without a review").

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ExtendedLineGame.StateTransport
+
+/-!
+# Pair-state consistency transport
+
+This module transports consistency defects on the two-player expanded state to
+the corresponding opposite placements on the six-register expanded state.
+
+## References
+
+These formalization-only identities support the application of `lem:pasting`
+in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963` and
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open scoped MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting
+
+/-- A consistency defect on the two-player expanded state equals the defect
+of the same measurements placed on `AA'` and `BA''` in the six-register state. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_pairState_eq_AA'_BA''
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    {Sample Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Sample] [DecidableEq Sample]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    (law : Distribution Sample)
+    (first : Sample → Measurement Outcome (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice))
+    (second : Sample → Measurement Outcome (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
+    consistencyDefect law
+        (fun sample answer => heteroKron ((first sample).effect answer) 1)
+        (fun sample answer => heteroKron 1 ((second sample).effect answer))
+        (ExtendedLineGame.pairState S) =
+      consistencyDefect law
+        (fun sample answer => S.place .AA' ((first sample).effect answer))
+        (fun sample answer => S.place .BA'' ((second sample).effect answer))
+        S.psiHat := by
+  classical
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro sample
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro firstAnswer _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro secondAnswer _

This file holds only\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\nrules never move here.\n\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\n\n### Linter warnings\n\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. Linters exist to expose real\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\n\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\n\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\n\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\n\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\n\n### Source-faithfulness checks\n\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\n\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\nmathematically load-bearing.\n\nReviewers should also inspect `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\n\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\n\n### Companion document\n\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\n\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\n\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\n`AGENTS.md`):\n\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\n> conditional helper\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\n\n### Axiom policy\n\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\nthe axiomatic base.\n\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\n\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\n\nSigns to watch for:\n\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\n  semantics (e.g., a \"projective measurement\" definition that does not enforce\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\n- Definitions that \"work\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\n  incompatible universes)\n\nWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\nthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\nprogress rather than enabling it.\n\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\n\nA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\nif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\nChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\n\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\ntheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\nrepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\n`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\ngeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\nassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\n\nConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\nbe closed. These\nconditions should still be reviewed. {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_3","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,280p' docs/anti_patterns.md\"","aggregated_output":"# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\n\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. Altogether the distance is $O(\\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[EPR projection estimates]\\label{thm:qld-epr-projection-estimates}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.norm_sub_eprProjection_le}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.idealExpState_extractionAux0}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.exists_unit_aux_near_eprProjection}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, lem:projective-strategy-setup}\n\tThis auxiliary statement isolates the projection and normalization\n\tcalculations in the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-unitary}.\n\tWrite $E=\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$ and\n\t\\[\n\t\tH_W=\\frac{1}{q^M}\\sum_{u\\in\\F_q^M}\\tau^W(u)\\ot\\tau^W(u).\n\t\\]\n\t\tlem:qld-evaluated-pauli-given-global-pair, lem:v-swap-conjugation,\n\t\tlem:qld-pauli-overlap-state-transfer,\n\t\tlem:qld-large-error-extraction-given-global-pair}\n\tLet $C_S,C_E$ be the universal constants in the auxiliary-state and\n\tevaluated-consistency estimates. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M})_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.\n\tThe numerical corrections and their role in the extraction argument are\n\tdocumented in \\cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}\n\nWe can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.\n\n\\begin{proof}\n\t\\proves{thm:pauli}\n\t\\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:qld-extraction-error-form, lem:pauli-completeness,\n\t\tthm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state,\n\t\tdef:EPR, def:povm-distance}\n\tLet $(\\ket{\\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \\eps$, where $\\ket{\\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\\mathrm{A}$ and $\\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\\ket{\\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. The present proof is therefore\n\tcomplete only modulo these four obligations. the range-projection\n\t% argument below supplies the missing step.\n\tItem~2 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, (M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}} \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger = V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\bigl(\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''} \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger$ onto the range of $\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\\mathrm{A}}$ and $\\bigl(\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, (M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger\n\t\t= V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\Bigl( (M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot \\bigl(\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''} \\Bigr) \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger\n\t\t= N^W_h \\, Q_{\\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, N^W_h\\;.\n\t\\]\n\tThe estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, (M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger$ as follows. Write $\\ket{\\Delta} = \\ket{\\mathrm{aux}} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$ and $\\ket{\\vartheta} = \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot \\phi_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\psi}$. Since $\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger \\phi_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\Id$, the projection $\\Id - Q_{\\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\\ket{\\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\bigl\\| (\\Id - Q_{\\mathrm{A}}) \\ket{\\Delta} \\bigr\\|^2\n\t\t= \\bigl\\| (\\Id - Q_{\\mathrm{A}}) (\\ket{\\Delta} - \\ket{\\vartheta}) \\bigr\\|^2\n\t\t\\leq \\bigl\\| \\ket{\\Delta} - \\ket{\\vartheta} \\bigr\\|^2\n\t\t\\leq \\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}\\;.\n\t\\]\n\tSince the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \\in \\F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\\sum_h \\| N^W_h \\ket{\\xi} \\|^2 = \\| \\ket{\\xi} \\|^2$ for every vector $\\ket{\\xi}$. This shows that the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}(\\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'$ with $\\mathrm{A}'$ and $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'$ with $\\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\\phi_{\\mathrm{A}}\\colon \\mathcal{H}_{\\mathrm{A}} \\to \\mathcal{H}_{\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\mathcal{H}_{\\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}(\\eps,m,d,q) = O(\\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\\delta_P = C(\\delta_G + \\sqrt{\\eps} + md/q)$ and $\\delta_G$ already has that form. This is the placement of the ideal Pauli operators in\n   123\tblueprint `lem:qld-unitary`, paper\n   124\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/\n   125\tnoncomputable def placeExtractedRegister (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)\n   126\t    (side : PlayerSide) (O : Op (PauliRegister P)) :\n   127\t    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by\n   128\t  cases side with\n   129\t  | alice =>\n   130\t      exact S.place .BA'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) O)\n   131\t  | bob =>\n   132\t      exact S.place .AB'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) O)\n   133\t\n   134\t/-- Place a pair of block operators simultaneously on `AA'A''` and\n   135\t`BB'B''`. This is the simultaneous placement used for the transformed state in\n   136\tblueprint `lem:qld-unitary`, paper\n   137\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/\n   138\tnoncomputable def placeBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)\n   139\t    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))\n   140\t    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :\n   141\t    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=\n   142\t  reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)\n   143\t    (heteroKron VA VB)\n   144\t\n   145\t/-- Apply one operator to each heterogeneous extraction block. This is the\n   146\twitness-independent state transformation used for `V_A tensor V_B` in\n   147\tblueprint `lem:qld-unitary`, paper\n   148\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/\n   149\tnoncomputable def applyBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)\n   150\t    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))\n   151\t    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))\n   152\t    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ\n   153\t      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :\n   154\t    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=\n   155\t  applyOperatorToState (S.placeBoth VA VB) ψ\n   156\t\n   157\t/-- The state `aux tensor EPR_q^{tensor M}` in the six-register order.\n   158\tThis is the ideal state in Item 1 of blueprint\n   159\t`lem:qld-unitary`, paper\n   160\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/\n   161\tnoncomputable def idealExpState (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)\n   162\t    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ\n   163\t      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :\n   164\t    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by\n   165\t  classical\n   166\t  exact\n   167\t    reindexState (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)\n   168\t      (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))\n   169\t\n   170\tend ProjectiveSetting\n   171\t\n   172\t/-! ## Coarse-grained Pauli projectors -/\n   173\t\n   174\t/-- Coarse-grain a finite operator family along a map of outcomes. This is the\n   175\toperator-valued sum corresponding to `Measurement.postprocess`, used by\n   176\tblueprint\n   177\t`def:tau-dot-product-projector`. -/\n   178\tnoncomputable def bracketOp {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]\n   179\t    (N : α → Op ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) : Op ι :=\n   180\t  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), N a\n   181\t\n   182\t/-- The effect of a postprocessed measurement is the corresponding\n   183\tcoarse-grained operator sum. This equality is used by blueprint `def:bracket`\n   184\tand `def:tau-dot-product-projector`. -/\n   185\ttheorem postprocess_effect_eq_bracketOp {α β ι : Type*}\n   186\t    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]\n   187\t    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :\n   188\t    (M.postprocess f).effect b = bracketOp M.effect f b :=\n   189\t  rfl\n   190\t\n   191\t/-- The projector obtained by measuring in basis `W` and retaining outcomes\n   192\twhose dot product with `u` is `a`. This is Equation `eq:def-tauwu` in\n   193\tblueprint\n   194\t`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, paper\n   195\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`. -/\n   196\tnoncomputable def tauDotProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)\n   197\t    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=\n   198\t  bracketOp (pauliProj W) (fun h => dotProduct h u) a\n   199\t\n   200\t/-- Each dot-product coarse-graining is a projector, as asserted in\n   201\tblueprint\n   202\t`lem:tau-dot-product-projective`, paper\n   203\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.\n   204\t\n   205\tCompleteness makes the matrix of Pauli basis vectors unitary. The coarse-grained\n   206\toperator is the conjugate of the diagonal projector onto the specified outcomes. -/\n   207\ttheorem tauDotProj_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)\n   208\t    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :\n   209\t    IsProj (tauDotProj W u a) := by\n   210\t  classical\n   211\t  let basisMatrix : Op (PauliRegister P) := fun row label => pauliVec W label row\n   212\t  have hbasis : basisMatrix * basisMatrixᴴ = 1 := by\n   213\t    calc\n   214\t      basisMatrix * basisMatrixᴴ = ∑ label : PauliRegister P, pauliProj W label := by\n   215\t        ext row column\n   216\t        simp [basisMatrix, Matrix.mul_apply, pauliProj, Matrix.sum_apply,\n   217\t          Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]\n   218\t      _ = 1 := sum_pauliProj_eq_one W\n   219\t  let diagonalProj : Op (PauliRegister P) :=\n   220\t    Matrix.diagonal (fun label => if dotProduct label u = a then (1 : ℂ) else 0)\n   221\t  have hdiagonal : IsProj diagonalProj := by\n   222\t    constructor\n   223\t    · change Matrix.diagonal _ * Matrix.diagonal _ = Matrix.diagonal _\n   224\t      rw [Matrix.diagonal_mul_diagonal]\n   225\t      congr 1\n   226\t      funext label\n   227\t      split_ifs <;> simp\n   228\t    · change diagonalProjᴴ = diagonalProj\n   229\t      simp [diagonalProj, Matrix.diagonal_conjTranspose]\n   230\t  have hcoarse : tauDotProj W u a = basisMatrix * diagonalProj * basisMatrixᴴ := by\n   231\t    ext row column\n   232\t    simp only [tauDotProj, bracketOp, Matrix.sum_apply, pauliProj, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]\n   233\t    rw [Matrix.mul_apply]\n   234\t    simp only [diagonalProj, Matrix.mul_diagonal]\n   235\t    simp [basisMatrix, Finset.sum_filter, mul_ite, ite_mul]\n   236\t  rw [hcoarse]\n   237\t  exact hdiagonal.map (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (Op (PauliRegister P))\n   238\t    ⟨basisMatrix, Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff.mpr hbasis⟩)\n   239\t\n   240\t/-- For fixed `W` and `u`, the dot-product projectors sum to the identity.\n   241\tThis is the completeness assertion of blueprint\n   242\t`lem:tau-dot-product-projective`, paper\n   243\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.\n   244\t\n   245\tThe dot-product fibers partition the complete Pauli outcome family. -/\n   246\ttheorem sum_tauDotProj_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)\n   247\t    (u : PauliRegister P) :\n   248\t    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tauDotProj W u a = 1 := by\n   249\t  classical\n   250\t  unfold tauDotProj bracketOp\n   251\t  rw [Finset.sum_fiberwise]\n   252\t  exact sum_pauliProj_eq_one W\n   253\t\n   254\topen scoped MatrixOrder ComplexOrder in\n   255\t/-- Distinct dot-product fibers give orthogonal coarse-grained Pauli projectors.\n   256\t\n   257\tThis formalization-only companion follows from projectivity and completeness\n   258\tusing the existing projective-measurement orthogonality theorem. The source\n   259\tdefinition is `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`. -/\n   260\ttheorem tauDotProj_mul_eq_zero_of_ne {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)\n   261\t    (u : PauliRegister P) {a b : PauliScalar P} (hab : a ≠ b) :\n   262\t    tauDotProj W u a * tauDotProj W u b = 0 := by\n   263\t  let M : Measurement (PauliScalar P) (PauliRegister P) :=\n   264\t    Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tauDotProj W u)\n   265\t      (fun c => (tauDotProj_isProj W u c).nonneg) (sum_tauDotProj_eq_one W u)\n   266\t  exact DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero\n   267\t    M (tauDotProj_isProj W u) hab\n   268\t\n   269\t/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/\n   270\t\n   271\t/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact\n   272\tconjugation equations in blueprint\n   273\t`lem:v-swap-conjugation`, paper\n   274\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/\n   275\tnoncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]\n   276\t    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=\n   277\t  V * N * Vᴴ\n   278\t\n   279\t/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from\n   280\ta global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The\n   281\tremaining terms record the point-measurement transfer\n   282\tand the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also\n   283\tdominates terms of order `epsilon`.\n   284\t\n   285\tThis makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in\n   286\tblueprint\n   287\t`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, paper\n   288\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/\n   289\tnoncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)\n   290\t    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=\n   291\t  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +\n   292\t    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))\n   293\t\n   294\t/-- The explicit extraction scale\n   295\t`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from blueprint\n   296\t`lem:qld-unitary`, paper\n   297\t`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/\n   298\tnoncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=\n   299\t  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))\n   300\t\n   301\tend\n   302\t\n   303\tend MIPStarRE.QPBT\n     1\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Defs\n     2\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree\n     3\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Consistency\n     4\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineMeasurement\n     5\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.WinImplications\n     6\t\n     7\t/-!\n     8\t# Witnesses for combining the Pauli bases\n     9\t\n    10\tThis module defines the five measurement and distribution witnesses used in\n    11\tthe combining argument.  Every measurement is indexed by the player side, so\n    12\tAlice's and Bob's local spaces remain distinct.  The extended-dimensional\n    13\tline objects use the directly indexed low-degree interface and therefore do\n    14\tnot require a dimension-divisibility hypothesis.\n    15\t\n    16\t## References\n    17\t\n    18\t`CombinedPointsWitness`, `CombinedLinesWitness`, and `GlobalPairWitness` record\n    19\tthe measurement conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10`, `lem:qld-xz-lines`, and\n    20\t`lem:qld-4-7`, respectively, in\n    21\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  `SubLineWitness` and\n    22\t`ExtendedLinesWitness` instead support `lem:qld-sublines` and `lem:qld-4-13`\n    23\tthrough the directly indexed extended-line carrier and probability law.  The\n    24\tlatter also uses the completed answer alphabet, rather than the field-valued\n    25\tanswer sum in the source statement.  The paper source is\n    26\t`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709,\n    27\t882-894,1020-1069,1267-1274`.\n    28\t-/\n    29\t\n    30\tnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n    31\t\n    32\topen MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement\n    33\topen MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries MIPStarRE.Quantum\n    34\t\n    35\tnoncomputable section\n    36\t\n    37\t/-! ## The canonical scalar identification -/\n    38\t\n    39\t/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar\n    40\tfield.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for\n    41\tadmissibility differs. -/\n    42\tnoncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :\n    43\t    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by\n    44\t  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _\n    45\t  cases h\n    46\t  exact RingEquiv.refl _\n    47\t\n    48\t/-- Transport an extended direct point into the canonical Pauli scalar field. -/\n    49\tdef directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)\n    50\t    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :\n    51\t    Fin (2 * P.m + 2) -> PauliScalar P :=\n    52\t  fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (u i)\n    53\t\n    54\t/-! ## Combined point and line measurements -/\n    55\t\n    56\t/-- Projective joint point measurements and their ordered consistency\n    57\tguarantees from `lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709. This file holds only\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\nrules never move here.\n\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\n\n### Linter warnings\n\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\n\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\n\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\n\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\n\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\n\n### Source-faithfulness checks\n\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`. A source-labelled\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\n\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\n\n### Companion document\n\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\n\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\n\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\n`AGENTS.md`):\n\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\n> conditional helper\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\n\n### Axiom policy\n\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\nthe axiomatic base.\n\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\n\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\n\nSigns to watch for:\n\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\n  semantics (e.g., a \"projective measurement\" definition that does not enforce\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\n- Definitions that \"work\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\n  incompatible universes)\n\nWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\nthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\nprogress rather than enabling it.\n\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\n\nA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\nif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\nChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\n\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\ntheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\nrepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\n`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\ngeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\nassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\n\nConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\nbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\nnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\nhelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\nobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\nthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\n`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\nblueprint theorem with `\\leanok`.\n\nExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\nfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\nstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\nbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\nto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\ntracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\n\nNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\nto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\ninstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\nfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\nconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\nmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\nstep of the source proof.\n\nFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Source-statement proof gaps\n\n**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\n[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\nproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\nstructure. Why the reviewer is chained to CI\n\nThe parent workflow's own header records the reason (`pr-review.yml:3-8`):\nthe predecessors `claude-code-review.yml` and `blueprint-prose-review.yml`\nfired on every push, so a pull request whose build was about to fail still\ndrew two full reviews per push — and the auto-fix loop then rewrote the very\ncode under review.  Chaining the review to CI completion spends review effort\nonly on code that at least compiles.\n\nLocally the chain is: `ci.sh` publishes the `local-ci/*` statuses on the head\nSHA; `review.sh` refuses to do anything until the `local-ci/summary` roll-up is\n`success` for the **current** head.  There is no event bus, so the chain is an\nordering discipline rather than a trigger, and the discipline is enforced by the\ngate below rather than by trust.\n\nMarking a draft ready is not a trigger there and is not one here.  A review\nfollows a CI run, and only a CI run.\n\n## 2. The gate\n\nThe gate is a ladder.  Each rung either passes, skips (exit 0, no verdict), or\n**blocks** (exit 3, publishing nothing at all — the *absence* of a green\n`local-review/summary` is the block).  The distinction between skip and\nblock is the whole point of the rung: `pr-review.yml:59-61` fails the job with\n\"PR CI concluded X; PR Review must not report success without a review\", a\nfail-instead-of-skip semantics that exists because a skipped review once read\nas a green one.\n\n| # | Rung | Outcome when it fires |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` is the literal string `false` | skip, exit 0 |\n| 2 | no open GitHub PR for the number, or no head SHA | error, exit 1 |\n| 3 | branch name contains `] ~ ^ : ? *`, space or backslash | error, exit 1 |\n| 4 | branch under review equals `MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF` | error, exit 1 |\n| 5 | `local-ci/summary` is missing on the head SHA, or is not `success` | **block**, exit 3 |\n| 6 | the local branch tip ≠ the remote PR head | error, exit 1 |\n| 7 | head commit subject matches `^\\[(claude\\|codex)-(auto\\|review)-fix\\]` | skip, exit 0, unless `--force-review` |\n| 8 | a fix lock is held for this branch | skip, exit 0 |\n| 9 | the head moved while this run queued for the review lock | skip, exit 0 |\n| 10 | the diff against the merge base is empty | skip, exit 0 |\n\nRung 1 is `vars.CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED` (`pr-review.yml:44-48`).  **Only the\nliteral string `false` disables it**; unset, empty, `\"0\"`, `\"no\"` and `\"False\"`\nall leave the reviewer enabled.  This is DESIGN.md invariant 4, and it is not a\nstylistic preference: a port that treats unset as false silently stops\nreviewing and reports nothing.\n\nRung 7 is the ping-pong guard, and §5 explains it.\n\nRung 5 reads exactly one status, the `local-ci/summary` roll-up `ci.sh` posts\nlast; it never iterates the per-step contexts. Trusted prompts\n\nThe reviewer persona and task prompt are read with\n\n    git show \"$MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF:.github/prompts/<file>\"\n\nnever from the checkout under review.  On GitHub this was a second\n`actions/checkout` of the default branch into `.trusted-actions/`\n(`pr-review.yml:140-146`), with every prompt path prefixed by that directory\n(`pr-review.yml:173-182`, `:248-252`).  The property being preserved is that a\npull request cannot edit the instructions given to its own reviewer.  A branch\nthat *is* the trusted ref is refused outright (rung 4), because for such a\nbranch the property is unsatisfiable.\n\n`MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF` defaults to `main`.  Repointing it at anything a\ncontributor can push to defeats the guard; if you must, record why in\n`results/telemetry/events.md`.\n\nTwo prompt pairs are used, verbatim:\n\n| Review | Persona | Task |\n|---|---|---|\n| code | `claude-code-review-system-prompt.md` | `claude-code-review-prompt.md` |\n| prose | `blueprint-prose-review-system-prompt.md` | `blueprint-prose-review-prompt.md` |\n\nTo each, `review.sh` appends a **local execution contract** — the only text it\nadds — which states that `gh`, `git push` and `mcp__github__*` do not exist,\nthat the working tree is read-only, where the diff and the checkout are, and\nwhat the output must look like (§6). Untrusted data\n\nThe diff is the material under review, which makes it the most likely carrier\nof an injection attempt.
