Review Checklist\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n   Run `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" <file>` to verify.\n\n2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and\n   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`\n   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.\n\n3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration\n   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from\n   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See\n   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local\n   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag\n   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical\n   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,\n   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file\n   under [audits/](../audits/).\n   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and\n   format in\n   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).\n   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second\n   public name.\n   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)\n   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or\n   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or\n   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.\n\n4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask\n   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See\n   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow\n   exception policy.\n\n5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved\n   metavariables.\n\n6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on\n   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.\n\n7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be\n   upstreamed to Mathlib?\n\n8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the\n   relevant arXiv paper(s).\n\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement\n   from the blueprint, add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags to the\n   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public\n   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record\n   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only\n   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal\n   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected\n   by `\\uses{...}`. See\n   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).\n   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or\n   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.\n   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,\n   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,\n   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional\n   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before\n   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as\n   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been\n   formalized.\n\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded\n   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that\n   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom\n   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See\n   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and\n   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.\n\n11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against\n   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure\n   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail\n   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),\n   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches\n   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),\n   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).\n   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.\n\n12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure\n   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,\n   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against\n   [proof_frontier_review.md](proof_frontier_review.md). A PR that only\n   repackages an assumption should not be described as proving the corresponding\n   paper step; it must name the missing obligation discharger or link the native\n   sub-issue that tracks it.  For source-labelled theorems, the preferred repair\n   is to extract any usable proof content into source-faithful lemmas and\n   restore the paper-aligned statement, even if the remaining proof is a tracked\n   `sorry` during the cleanup.  For source-labelled proof gaps, also use the\n   protocol in\n   [paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).\n\n### Semantic scaffold checklist (required for core math objects)\n\nFor semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,\naveraged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally\nverify:\n\n1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are\n   impossible under the paper definition?\n2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived\n   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored\n   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?\n3. **Invariant bundling check** -- Are core invariants (positivity,\n   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly\n   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?\n4. **Stress-test check** -- Is at least one nontrivial theorem in scope of the\n   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?\n\nIf any answer is \"no\", treat the scaffold as unsafe and request a follow-up\nbefore broad theorem layering continues.\n\n---\n\n## 6. It governs how the protocols themselves\nchange, and the telemetry duties that make the project usable as research data.\n\n## Standing principles\n\n1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol\n   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the\n   protocol (or stops), records the friction in\n   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment — a dispatched\n   worker proposes it to the operator; the operator amends directly under the\n   procedure below, an `events.md` incident being a sufficient trigger.  Owner\n   sign-off is needed only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.\n2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under\n   `local/protocols/` or to `AGENTS.md` must append an entry to\n   `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` citing its trigger: an `events.md` incident,\n   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in\n   `builds.jsonl`), or an upstream policy decision by the user. No trigger,\n   no amendment.\n3. **The parent repo is precedent, not law.** The GitHub-era mechanism (frozen\n   under `.github/`, mapped in `local/DESIGN.md`) is the default answer to\n   \"how should this work?\"; deviations are fine when the local setting\n   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.\n4. **De-automation is a valid evolution step.** The parent workflow repeatedly\n   demoted LLM agents to deterministic scripts once the mechanical half of a\n   job was understood (issue-automation.yml:13-21), and demoted CI jobs to\n   notices when resources were exhausted. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that\n   holds the invariant.\n5. **Two memory disciplines.** Reports and session records are append-only and\n   never rewritten (supersede with dated status notes). Protocol documents\n   and paper-gap notes are living documents that are rewritten in place\n   (history lives in git and `EVOLUTION.md`). Do not mix the two.\n\n## Amendment procedure\n\n1. Write the incident/observation in `results/telemetry/events.md` (dated).\n2. Draft the protocol edit.\n3. Append to `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`:\n   `## YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>` with fields **Trigger** (cite events.md\n   entry or telemetry line), **Change** (files + gist), **Expected effect**,\n   and, when known later, **Outcome**.\n4. Commit protocol edit and ledger entry together, `docs(local)` scope.\n5. If the change alters guard semantics (locks, caps, gates, kill switches),\n   grep `local/` for every enforcement point and update all of them in the\n   same commit — the parent repo maintained such consistency invariants\n   through cross-referencing comments; we inherit the same drift risk.\n\n## Telemetry duties\n\nSchemas (all JSONL, one object per line; timestamps ISO-8601 with offset):\n\n- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` —\n  `{ts, stage, event: start|end|milestone, note?, tokens_note?}`\n  Stages: `1-skeleton`, `2-references`, `3-blueprint`, `4.1-minimal`,\n  `4.2-full-skeleton`, `4.3-proofs` (extend as needed).\n- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` —\n  `{name, role, model?, account?, requested_effort?, issue, pr?, thread_id,\n    start, end, wall_s, usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},\n    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`\n  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`. New dispatches always\n  supply `account` (`primary` or `second`) and the exact resolved `model`\n  passed to the CLI (environment override, otherwise selected-account config).\n  External rows use allocator accounts `primary|second`; native rows use the\n  active key label (`space` or historical `relay-1`) in both `account` and\n  `key_label`, with `dispatcher: native`.\n  When the dispatcher supplies a reasoning override, `requested_effort` is its\n  effective value after model-specific normalization. It records the CLI request,\n  not provider-measured effort. All three fields remain optional for historical\n  rows and legacy replay callers.\n- `results/telemetry/owner-sessions.jsonl` —\n  `{name, role, model, issue, pr?, worktree?, base?, start, end?, wall_s?,\n    status, tokens?, tool_uses?, findings_fixed?, commits?, note?}`.\n  Written only by the owner session and `/tmp/claude-lane-prep.sh` /\n  `/tmp/claude-lane-finish.sh`; `tokens` is the harness-reported subagent total.\n  For `role: mathfix`, `issue` identifies the gap whose shared budget is charged.\n- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` —\n  `{ts, kind: warm|rebuild|cache-get|ci-build, trigger, seconds, outcome,\n    sha?, note?}`\n- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated bullets; free prose; one incident per\n  bullet: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.\n\nDuties:\n\n- **Every external Codex session goes through `dispatch.sh`** so token usage and wall\n  time land in `sessions.jsonl`. A session started any other way is a\n  telemetry hole; if one happens, backfill a line with `dispatcher: manual`.\n- Historical native descendants were recorded with `telemetry.py native-record`\n  under `sessions.md`:\n  `dispatcher: native`, root/parent IDs, key label, actual model/requested effort,\n  worktree, timestamps and status. `observed_usage` preserves raw cumulative rollout\n  counters, but `usage` remains null with `usage_scope: unknown`; parent inclusion\n  of descendants is unverified. Never convert missing usage to zero or sum these\n  observations. Private homes and credential data are not serialized. Requested\n  CLI Ultra is distinct from wire/returned Max seen in owner migration receipts;\n  absent request-specific wire evidence stays null, not inferred from configuration.\n- **Every full build** (warmer, CI, cold rebuild) lands in `builds.jsonl`.\n- **Stage transitions** are logged by the orchestrator (main session) at the\n  moment they happen, not reconstructed later.\n- Claude-side (non-Codex) subagent fleets are recorded in\n  `owner-sessions.jsonl` and summarized into `stages.jsonl` as `milestone`\n  entries with token totals, since they bypass `dispatch.sh`.\n\n## Research-data invariants\n\nModel-policy records (#301) retain `requested_model`, `selected_model`,\n`effective_model` only when observed, `job_class`, and `model_policy` with\nroutine/hard classification and the explicit hardness/escalation rationale.\nExternal capture without model evidence records effective model as null, not the\nCLI argument. Historical native observations retain all bound current-turn contexts; mixed\nmodels/efforts and requested/observed mismatches fail closed. Prior/forked contexts\nare not attributed to a new job. Requested effort remains distinct from provider\neffort; missing usage remains unknown and historical records are not rewritten.\n`dispatch_kind` is new/resume/grandfathered; `activation_at` fixes the accounting\nboundary. Ratio reports count actual distinct new threads with matching observed\nand selected models, with a rolling 100-dispatch window and separate cumulative\ncounts. Unknowns may resolve from later observations; conflicts remain unknown.\nMain, pre-activation workers and resumes do not count. Preserve predecessor and\ncumulative-budget links recorded when a model change required a fresh native identity.\n\nThe project doubles as a study of a self-evolving formalization workflow.\nThree artifacts must therefore stay trustworthy:\n\n- `EVOLUTION.md` — complete: every protocol change has an entry.\n- `events.md` — honest: failures are recorded as failures, including agent\n  mistakes, wasted builds, and reverted work.\n- `sessions.jsonl` + `stages.jsonl` — quantitative: per-stage cost\n  (time, tokens, session counts) reconstructible by a script, not by memory.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The symmetric equivalents follow by the same argument with the register bipartitions interchanged.\n \\end{proof}\n \n \\section{The swap unitaries and the extraction of the Pauli group}\n \n \\begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\\label{def:v-swap-unitary}\n \t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary}\n \t\\leanok\n \t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder}\n \tDefine the linear map\n \t\\[\n \t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\bigl(\\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\\;,\n \t\\]\n \twhere $\\tau^X(\\cdot)$ and $\\tau^Z(\\cdot)$ are the generalized Pauli observables acting on $(\\C^q)^{\\ot M}$; note that the argument of $\\tau^X$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\\tau^Z$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)$. The missing composition and the range-projection\n \ttransfer are recorded in \\cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.\n \\end{lemma}\n \\begin{proof}\n \t\\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}\n \tFor the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\\E_{j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}} \\E_{\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^M} \\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$; setting $\\ket{\\vartheta} = V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\hat\\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\\bra{\\vartheta} H_W \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$ for $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, where $H_W = \\E_j \\E_{\\tilde{u}} \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = \\bigl( \\E_{s \\in \\F_q} \\tau^W(s) \\ot \\tau^W(s) \\bigr)^{\\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\\tau^W(\\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \\mapsto e_j s$. the vacuous quantifier is dropped here.\n   229\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   230\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, on average over uniformly random $u \\in \\F_q^m$,\n   231\t\t\t\\[\n   232\t\t\t\t\\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''} \\ot \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \\simeq_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{AB}}} M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \\ot \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''}\n   233\t\t\t\\]\n   234\t\t\tand\n   235\t\t\t\\[\n   236\t\t\t\t\\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \\ot \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''} \\simeq_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{BA}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''} \\ot M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\\;,\n   237\t\t\t\\]\n   238\t\t\twith the answer summation over $a \\in \\F_q$.\n   239\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Self-consistency}) For all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$ and $j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}$, on average over uniformly random $\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^{M}$,\n   240\t\t\t\\[\n   241\t\t\t\t\\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ot \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''} \\approx_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{obs}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''} \\ot \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u})\\;.\n   242\t\t\t\\]\n   243\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   244\t\\end{lemma}\n   245\t\\begin{proof}\n   246\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper, def:expanded-point-measurement, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, lem:qld-decoder-evaluation, lem:qld-decoder-linearity, def:indicator-vector, lem:qld-win-implications, lem:qld-comm-cons, fact:add-a-proj, fact:agreement, fact:triangle, fact:data-processing, def:bracket, lem:povm-to-obs, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}\n   247\t\t% Support restriction added: the source (line 1492 of\n   248\t\t% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) rewrites Dec(g).ind_m(u) as\n   249\t\t% g(u) for every outcome g; This bound must be derived from point consistency and\n   296\t\tSchwartz--Zippel; it is not an additional extraction hypothesis.\n   297\t\\end{lemma}\n   298\t\n   299\t% Following the source, the next lemma is stated after\n   300\t% lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, whose proof invokes it; its own proof\n   301\t% depends only on lem:qld-4-7 and lem:qld-comm-cons, so there is no\n   302\t% circularity.\n   303\tLemmas~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7} and~\\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} imply the following two estimates, which were used in the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}.\n   304\t\n   305\t\\begin{lemma}[The marginals absorb the point measurements]\\label{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper}\n   306\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_marginalPoly_pointMeas_approx_id}\n   307\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.marginalPoly_sub_pointMeas_approx_zero}\n   308\t\t\\leanok\n   309\t\t\\uses{def:s-w-marginals, def:expanded-point-measurement, def:expanded-state, def:povm-distance, lem:qld-4-7, def:symmetric-equivalents}\n   310\t\tFor $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, on average over uniformly random $u \\in \\F_q^m$,\n   311\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-sg-cons}\n   312\t\t\t\\sum_g (\\hat{S}^W_g)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{g(u)})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''} \\approx_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{id}}} \\Id\n   313\t\t\\end{equation}\n   314\t\tand\n   315\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-sg-cons2}\n   316\t\t\t\\bigl(\\hat{S}^W_g \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ann}}} 0\\;,\n   317\t\t\\end{equation}\n   318\t\twhere the answer summation is over $g \\in \\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$. Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold (Definition~\\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}).\n   319\t\\end{lemma}\n   320\t\\begin{proof}\n   321\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, fact:agreement, fact:add-a-proj, def:bracket, lem:qld-comm-cons}\n   322\t\tThe point-consistency conclusion of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7} states that, on average over $u \\in \\F_q^m$,\n   323\t\t\\[\n   324\t\t\t\\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\sum_g (\\hat{S}^W_g)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''} \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\geq 1 - \\delta_G\\;,\n   325\t\t\\]\n   326\t\twhich says exactly that the operator on the left-hand side of \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons} is $\\delta_G$-consistent with $\\Id$; Lemma~\\ref{fact:agreement} and the universal-factor enlargement give the $\\approx_{\\delta_P}$ statement \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons}. For \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}, the same consistency, written with the coarse-graining $\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} = \\sum_{g : g(u) = a} \\hat{S}^W_g$ as $(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{O(\\delta_G)} (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''}$ with answer summation over $a \\in \\F_q$, is left-multiplied by $(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'}$ using Lemma~\\ref{fact:add-a-proj}; moving $\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ from registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''$ to $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'$ costs a further $\\eps$ by Cauchy--Schwarz together with the self-consistency of the $\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ (Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}), giving\n   327\t\t\\[\n   328\t\t\t(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{O(\\delta_G + \\eps)} (\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \\cdot \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'}\\;.\n   329\t\t\\]\n   330\t\tExpanding\n   331\t\t\\[\n   332\t\t\t\\E_u \\sum_g \\bigl\\| (\\hat{S}^W_{g} \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\bigr\\|^2\n   333\t\t\t= \\E_u \\sum_a \\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\bigl((\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a}) \\cdot \\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ket{\\hat\\psi}\n   334\t\t\\]\n   335\t\tand bounding the right-hand side by $O(\\delta_G + \\eps)$ using the two approximations above yields \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} at scale $\\delta_P$. The symmetric equivalents follow by the same argument with the register bipartitions interchanged.\n   336\t\\end{proof}\n   337\t\n   338\t\\section{The swap unitaries and the extraction of the Pauli group}\n   339\t\n   340\t\\begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\\label{def:v-swap-unitary}\n   341\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary}\n   342\t\t\\leanok\n   343\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder}\n   344\t\tDefine the linear map\n   345\t\t\\[\n   346\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\bigl(\\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\\;,\n   347\t\t\\]\n   348\t\twhere $\\tau^X(\\cdot)$ and $\\tau^Z(\\cdot)$ are the generalized Pauli observables acting on $(\\C^q)^{\\ot M}$; note that the argument of $\\tau^X$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\\tau^Z$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)$. The map $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$, acting on registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$, is defined analogously.\n   349\t\\end{definition}\n   350\t\n   351\t% In the source the following properties are established inline with the\n   352\t% definition of the swap unitaries; they are recorded here as a lemma.\n   353\t\\begin{lemma}[Unitarity and conjugation action of the swap unitaries]\\label{lem:v-swap-conjugation}\n   354\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose}\n   355\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary}\n   356\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs}\n   357\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeM}\n   358\t\t\\leanok\n   359\t\t\\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-w-observables, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:generalized-pauli, def:indicator-vector, def:bracket}\n   360\t\tThe maps $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:v-swap-unitary} are unitaries acting on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ and $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$ respectively, and their conjugation action is exact, as follows. For all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, $j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}$, and $\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^M$,\n   361\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}\n   362\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\bigl( \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\n   363\t\t\t\\qquad \\text{and} \\qquad\n   364\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\bigl( \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   365\t\t\\end{equation}\n   366\t\tand for all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, $u \\in \\F_q^m$, and $a \\in \\F_q$,\n   367\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}\n   368\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   369\t\t\t\\qquad\n   370\t\t\t\\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \\sum_{h \\,:\\, g_h(u) = a} \\tau^W_h\\;,\n   371\t\t\\end{equation}\n   372\t\ttogether with the analogous identity for $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$.\n   373\t\\end{lemma}\n   374\t\\begin{proof}\n   375\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:twisted-commutation, def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:indicator-vector, def:decoding-map, def:generalized-pauli}\n   376\t\tSince the measurement $\\{\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\\}$ is projective (Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and the $\\tau^X, \\tau^Z$ observables are self-inverse,\n   377\t\t\\[\n   378\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger = \\sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}''} = \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''}\\;,\n   379\t\t\\]\n   380\t\tand the same computation gives $V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger V_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\Id$, so $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ is unitary; likewise $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$. For \\eqref{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}, conjugate the product form \\eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} of $\\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u})$ (Lemma~\\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}): by the orthogonality of the projectors $\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, only the diagonal terms survive, and the twisted commutation relation (Lemma~\\ref{lem:twisted-commutation})\n   381\t\t\\[\n   382\t\t\t\\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)) \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\\tr( e_j(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \\cdot \\tilde{u}))} \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\, \\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\n   383\t\t\\]\n   384\t\tcancels the sign $(-1)^{\\tr(e_j (\\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \\cdot \\tilde{u}))}$ term by term, leaving $\\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = \\Id \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u})$. For \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, expand $\\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$ by \\eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \\eqref{eq:def-tauwu}; by the orthogonality of the $\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, conjugation replaces, in the term of $\\hat{S}^W_g$, each projector $\\tau^W_h$ by $\\tau^W_{h + \\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$, using the identities $\\tau^X(s)\\, \\tau^Z_h \\,\\tau^X(s)^\\dagger = \\tau^Z_{h+s}$ and $\\tau^Z(s)\\, \\tau^X_h\\, \\tau^Z(s)^\\dagger = \\tau^X_{h+s}$. Substituting $h' = h + \\mathrm{Dec}(g)$ turns the constraint $h \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = (\\mathrm{Dec}(g) \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u)) - a$ into $h' \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = -a = a$, since $\\F_q$ has characteristic $2$; the quantity $\\mathrm{Dec}(g) \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly, so no relation between it and $g(u)$ is used (Remark~\\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}). Since $h' \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_{h'}(u)$ \\eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}, summing over $g$ gives \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}; the computation for $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ is identical.\n   385\t\\end{proof}\n   386\t\n   387\t\\begin{lemma}[Extraction of the EPR state and the Pauli observables]\\label{lem:qld-unitary}\n   388\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ExtractionWitness}\n   389\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaExtract}\n   390\t\t\\notready\n   391\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:v-swap-unitary, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}\n   392\t\tThere is a universal constant $C_{\\mathrm{ext}}\\geq1$. Set\n   393\t\t\\[\n   394\t\t\t\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ext}}=C_{\\mathrm{ext}}B,\n   395\t\t\t\\qquad\n   396\t\t\t\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}=C_{\\mathrm{ext}}\n   397\t\t\t\\left((\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ext}})^{1/4}+\\frac{md}{q}\\right).\n   398\t\t\\]\n   399\t\tThere exist unitaries $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ acting on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ acting on registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$, such that the following hold.\n   400\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   401\t\t\t\\item There exists a state $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'$ such that\n   402\t\t\t\\[\n   403\t\t\t\t\\bigl\\| V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\hat{\\psi}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''} - \\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\bigr\\|^2 \\leq \\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}\\;.\n   404\t\t\t\\]\n   405\t\t\t\\item For $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$,\n   406\t\t\t\\begin{align*}\n   407\t\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\bigl(M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger &\\approx_{\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\\;, \\\\\n   408\t\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\bigl(M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger &\\approx_{\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   409\t\t\t\\end{align*}\n   410\t\t\twhere the $\\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''}$, with the answer summation over $h \\in \\F_q^{M}$ and no average over questions.\n   411\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   412\t\tThe unitaries may be taken to be $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:v-swap-unitary}.\n   413\t\tThe conditional result below assumes the global polynomial-pair measurement\n   414\t\tof Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whereas the present proof obtains that measurement\n   415\t\tfrom the lemma. It therefore establishes the extraction conclusions only\n   416\t\tafter the measurement and its consistency estimates are supplied, not the\n   417\t\texistence claim above. The missing composition and the range-projection\n   418\t\ttransfer are recorded in \\cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.\n   419\t\\end{lemma}\n   420\t\\begin{proof}\n   421\t\t\\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}\n   422\t\tFor the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\\E_{j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}} \\E_{\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^M} \\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$; setting $\\ket{\\vartheta} = V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\hat\\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\\bra{\\vartheta} H_W \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$ for $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, where $H_W = \\E_j \\E_{\\tilde{u}} \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = \\bigl( \\E_{s \\in \\F_q} \\tau^W(s) \\ot \\tau^W(s) \\bigr)^{\\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\\tau^W(\\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \\mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\\E_{s,s'} \\tau^X(s)\\tau^Z(s') \\ot \\tau^X(s)\\tau^Z(s') = \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$. The bounds $\\| (\\Id - H_W)\\ket{\\vartheta} \\|^2 \\leq \\delta_P$ and $\\bra{\\vartheta} H_W^2 \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - 2\\delta_P$, combined through the triangle inequality $\\| H_X \\ket{\\vartheta} - H_Z \\ket{\\vartheta} \\| \\leq 2\\sqrt{\\delta_P}$ (see Remark~\\ref{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}), give $\\bra{\\vartheta} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M})_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - 4\\delta_P$.\n   423\t\t% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector\n   424\t\t% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.\n   425\t\tIf $\\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\\delta_P \\leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M})_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\\delta_P \\geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\\ket{\\vartheta}$ with $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\\sqrt{1 - 4\\delta_P} \\geq 1 - 4\\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\\delta_P = O(\\sqrt{\\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \\in \\F_q^m$, $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \\ot \\Id \\simeq_\\eps \\Id \\ot M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\\Id \\ot M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \\simeq_\\eps M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \\ot \\Id$, where $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \\sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\\eps \\leq \\sqrt{\\eps} \\leq \\delta_P$, yields $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \\ot \\Id \\simeq_{\\sqrt{\\delta_P}} \\Id \\ot \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Writing $\\ket{\\Delta} = \\ket{\\mathrm{aux}} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$, the quantity to be bounded for the $\\mathrm{A}$-side relation equals $2 - 2\\sum_h \\bra{\\Delta} V_{\\mathrm{A}} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\Delta}$, since $(\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{A}''} \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M} = (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$. Replacing $(\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\\E_u \\sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\\tau^W_{h'})_{\\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \\neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \\neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\\E_u \\sum_{a} \\bra{\\Delta} V_{\\mathrm{A}} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger \\ket{\\Delta}$. Exchanging $\\ket{\\Delta}$ for $\\ket{\\vartheta}$ costs $O(\\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\\E_u \\sum_a \\bra{\\hat\\psi} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \\ot \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \\ket{\\hat\\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\\sqrt{\\delta_P})$ by the $\\simeq_{\\sqrt{\\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.\n   426\t\\end{proof}\n   427\t\n   428\t\\begin{theorem}[EPR projection estimates]\\label{thm:qld-epr-projection-estimates}\n   429\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr}\n   430\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.norm_sub_eprProjection_le}\n   431\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.idealExpState_extractionAux0}\n   432\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.exists_unit_aux_near_eprProjection}\n   433\t\t\\leanok\n   434\t\t\\uses{def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, lem:projective-strategy-setup}\n   435\t\tThis auxiliary statement isolates the projection and normalization\n   436\t\tcalculations in the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-unitary}.\n   437\t\tWrite $E=\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$ and\n   438\t\t\\[\n   439\t\t\tH_W=\\frac{1}{q^M}\\sum_{u\\in\\F_q^M}\\tau^W(u)\\ot\\tau^W(u).\n   440\t\t\\]\n   441\t\tThen $H_XH_Z=\\ket{E}\\bra{E}$. Let $R$ be an auxiliary register and\n   442\t\t$\\vartheta$ a unit vector on $R\\ot A''\\ot B''$. If $\\delta\\geq0$ and\n   443\t\t\\[\n   444\t\t\t\\Re\\langle\\vartheta,(\\Id_R\\ot H_W)\\vartheta\\rangle\n   445\t\t\t\\geq1-\\delta/2\\qquad(W\\in\\{X,Z\\}),\n   446\t\t\\]\n   447\t\tthen, writing $\\Pi=\\Id_R\\ot\\ket{E}\\bra{E}$, one has\n   448\t\t\\[\n   449\t\t\t\\|\\vartheta-\\Pi\\vartheta\\|\\leq2\\sqrt\\delta.\n   450\t\t\\]\n   451\t\tIn the projective setting of Lemma~\\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup},\n   452\t\ttake $R=AA'BB'$. For every unit vector $\\vartheta$ on the six registers,\n   453\t\tset $\\mathrm{aux}_0=(\\Id_R\\ot\\bra{E})\\vartheta$. Then\n   454\t\t$\\mathrm{aux}_0\\ot E=\\Pi\\vartheta$, and there is a unit vector\n   455\t\t$\\mathrm{aux}$ on $R$ such that\n   456\t\t\\[\n   457\t\t\t\\|\\vartheta-\\mathrm{aux}\\ot E\\|\n   458\t\t\t\\leq2\\|\\vartheta-\\Pi\\vartheta\\|.\n   459\t\t\\]\n   460\t\\end{theorem}\n   461\t\\begin{proof}\n   462\t\t\\leanok\n   463\t\t\\uses{lem:pauli-observable-expansion, def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR}\n   464\t\tFourier inversion shows that $H_Z$ keeps precisely the equal computational\n   465\t\tlabels. Authoritative source for category B: `docs/mathematical_language.md`. Read it once

## Category A — 🟡 Blueprint ↔ Lean equivalence and status

This is the **core** check. The blueprint must not merely *link* to a Lean
declaration via `\lean{...}` — it must state the **same mathematical
content**, and its `\leanok` / `\notready` status tags must reflect
reality. `leanblueprint checkdecls` only verifies that tags resolve; YOU
verify they are *correct*.

For every `\lean{Namespace.Name}` tag in a `.tex` file changed in this PR,
and for every Lean declaration added or modified in this PR that has a
blueprint counterpart, do the following four checks:

### A.1 — Mathematical equivalence

Read the blueprint statement in `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` and the
corresponding Lean declaration in `MIPStarRE/...`. Compare them on every
axis that matters:

- **Quantifiers and hypotheses.** Does every blueprint hypothesis appear
  in the Lean signature, with the same strength? Watch for silent
  weakening ("primitive" in blueprint vs "irreducible" in Lean) or
  silent strengthening ("for all $A$" in blueprint vs implicit
  `[Nontrivial A]`/`[Fintype d]`/etc. in Lean that the blueprint
  omits).
  For a theorem, lemma, or proposition that cites a paper statement,
  an additional bridge, residual, repair, package, producer, witness, wrapper, proof-obligation input, or generic hypotheses bundle, generic assumptions bundle, or arbitrary
  hypothesis input is a mathematical mismatch. The only acceptable extra
  hypotheses are boundary conditions genuinely needed to state the same
  mathematics in Lean, such as positivity for a division, nonemptiness,
  decidability, or a field-model instance. Proof-debt objects are not
  boundary conditions.
  Missing proof work belongs as a tracked `sorry` on the source-faithful
  theorem, as a source-faithful lemma target to be proved from the same
  hypotheses, or as a paper-gap report; it must not become a bundled hypothesis
  consumed by downstream code.  Do not recommend adding a conditional helper
  merely to make a blueprint link pass.  An existing conditional helper may
  remain only as temporary quarantine for already useful proof content, with an
  explicit discharge or deletion plan, and it must stay off the paper theorem's
  `\leanok` path.
- **Conclusion.** Does the blueprint conclusion match the Lean return
  type? Watch for "$X$" vs "$X^\dagger$", "$=$" vs "$\leq$", strict
  vs non-strict inequalities, and conjugate-linear vs linear conventions
  (e.g. `mpvOverlap A B N = star (mpvInner A B N)` — the project's own
  `Fact-Check Lessons` in `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` calls this out).
- **Indexing conventions.** Blueprint indices run 0 to d−1 (matching
  `Fin d`). Flag if the blueprint silently uses 1 to d.
- **Definitions vs theorems.** If the blueprint asserts a fact ("X is a
  subalgebra"), it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not
  `\begin{definition}`.
- **Notation drift.** Does the blueprint use the established notation
  from `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` §"Notation Consistency"? Ad-hoc
  notation that disagrees with the Lean object is a sync bug.

For each mismatch, cite both the blueprint line and the Lean line, and
describe the mathematical discrepancy precisely. Do NOT accept "close
enough" — sync means equivalence, not similarity.

The section below is .github/prompts/claude-code-review-prompt.md, verbatim.

Use `gh pr diff <PR_NUMBER>` to see the changes.

Focus your review on the categories below. Each category has a severity level
that determines whether the PR can be approved with outstanding issues.

**Severity levels:**
- 🔴 **Blocker** — must be fixed before merge. Request changes if any are found.
- 🟡 **Requires changes** — must be addressed before approval. These are NOT nits.
  Do NOT approve the PR while issues in this category remain unresolved.
- ℹ️ **Advisory** — flag for awareness, acceptable with justification.

---

1. 🔴 **Proof integrity**: Read the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the complete list of proof
   integrity rules. Flag **blockers** as must-fix issues that should block merge. Flag
   **warnings** as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be acceptable with justification.
   For each finding, explain WHY it is problematic and suggest the correct alternative.
2. 🔴 **Proof correctness**: Are proof terms well-structured? Do tactic proofs follow a logical
   strategy, or are they brute-forced with `simp` / `omega` / `ring` chains? Are `calc` blocks
   and `conv` rewrites correctly chained? Are hypotheses used or dangling?
   If a mathematical result looks wrong, too strong, or suspiciously general, **scout** the
   source hierarchy: first `references/ldt-paper/`, then the corresponding blueprint material
   in `blueprint/src/chapter/`. Read the relevant sections, compare hypotheses and conclusions,
   and cite the specific source path, label, and line when flagging a discrepancy.
3. 🔴 **Source-statement fidelity**: For every changed theorem, lemma, or definition that is
   named after a paper result, linked from the blueprint by `\lean{...}`, or described as a
   formalization of a cited result, compare its public Lean statement with the corresponding
   statement in `references/ldt-paper/`. Flag any added load-bearing hypothesis, weakened
   conclusion, changed error parameter, or altered quantifier structure. In particular,
   bridge, residual, repair, package, producer, witness, wrapper, proof-obligation input,
   hypotheses bundle, assumptions bundle, or
   arbitrary implication hypotheses are blockers unless they are explicitly part of the
   paper statement or are documented Lean boundary conditions needed to state the
   mathematics, such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, or field-model hypotheses.
   Proof-debt bundles are not boundary conditions.
   If such data are still needed, the paper theorem must remain source-faithful and the
   missing proof should remain as a tracked `sorry`, a source-faithful lemma target to be
   proved from the same hypotheses, or a paper-gap report.  Do not accept a conditional
   helper as the default repair path.
   Existing conditional helpers must have names that make the conditional nature clear,
   cite the unresolved source obligation, state a removal plan, and must not be treated as
   the paper theorem or advertised by `\leanok`.
   A newly introduced conditional helper, proof-debt bundle, producer, witness, wrapper, or obligation
   package is itself a blocker unless the PR is explicitly a paper-realignment change,
   the new object preserves useful proof content from an already drifting statement, and
   the paper-facing theorem remains source-faithful.
4. 🟡 **Mathlib style**: Does the code follow Mathlib conventions? Check naming (`camelCase` for
   defs, `snake_case` for lemmas), tactic style (prefer `exact` over `apply` + `rfl` when
   equivalent), import hygiene (no unnecessary `open`s, minimal imports), and lemma placement.
   Style violations are NOT nits — they must be fixed before approval.
5. 🔴 **Type safety**: Any type mismatches, universe issues, or coercion problems? Check for
   universe polymorphism issues, missing `[DecidableEq]` or `[Fintype]` instances, and
   coercion chains that may cause unification failures.
6. 🟡 **Performance**: Will any proofs cause timeouts? Watch for `decide` on large types,
   `simp` with unbounded lemma sets, deep `rw` chains, and `norm_num` on symbolic expressions.
   Suggest alternatives like `omega`, `positivity`, or explicit `calc` steps.
   Performance issues that will likely cause timeouts must be fixed before approval.
7. 🟡 **Modularity & duplication**: Are new lemmas general enough? Could any be upstreamed to
   Mathlib? Are there lemmas that are overly specialized to the local context but could be
   stated more generally? Is the file structure consistent with the existing module hierarchy?
   Flag duplicated logic or lemmas that restate existing Mathlib results.
   Modularity and duplication issues must be fixed before approval.
8. 🟡 **Documentation**: Do new definitions and key theorems have docstrings? Are module-level
   doc comments present for new files? Do docstrings explain mathematical meaning, not just
   Lean syntax? Missing documentation must be added before approval.
   Blueprint citations in Lean docstrings are stored by label (for example,
   blueprint `lem:cl-concat`), while their current file and line span are
   derived with `scripts/blueprint_citations.py`. If the label resolves to the
   intended node, do not flag line drift or demand a stored numeric blueprint
   range. Unknown, duplicate, or mathematically incorrect labels still require
   correction.
9. 🟡 **Blueprint coverage for changed declarations**: If the PR has the label
   `enforce-blueprint-coverage` and changes a public paper-facing `def`,
   `theorem`, or `lemma` under `MIPStarRE/`, the corresponding blueprint item
   should carry the appropriate `\lean{...}` tag. You may run
   `python3 scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py --root . --warn-missing-blueprint

## Category A — 🟡 Blueprint ↔ Lean equivalence and status

This is the **core** check. The blueprint must not merely *link* to a Lean
declaration via `\lean{...}` — it must state the **same mathematical
content**, and its `\leanok` / `\notready` status tags must reflect
reality. `leanblueprint checkdecls` only verifies that tags resolve; YOU
verify they are *correct*.

For every `\lean{Namespace.Name}` tag in a `.tex` file changed in this PR,
and for every Lean declaration added or modified in this PR that has a
blueprint counterpart, do the following four checks:

### A.1 — Mathematical equivalence

Read the blueprint statement in `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` and the
corresponding Lean declaration in `MIPStarRE/...`. Compare them on every
axis that matters:

- **Quantifiers and hypotheses.** Does every blueprint hypothesis appear
  in the Lean signature, with the same strength? Watch for silent
  weakening ("primitive" in blueprint vs "irreducible" in Lean) or
  silent strengthening ("for all $A$" in blueprint vs implicit
  `[Nontrivial A]`/`[Fintype d]`/etc. in Lean that the blueprint
  omits).
  For a theorem, lemma, or proposition that cites a paper statement,
  an additional bridge, residual, repair, package, producer, witness, wrapper, proof-obligation input, or generic hypotheses bundle, generic assumptions bundle, or arbitrary
  hypothesis input is a mathematical mismatch. The only acceptable extra
  hypotheses are boundary conditions genuinely needed to state the same
  mathematics in Lean, such as positivity for a division, nonemptiness,
  decidability, or a field-model instance. Proof-debt objects are not
  boundary conditions.
  Missing proof work belongs as a tracked `sorry` on the source-faithful
  theorem, as a source-faithful lemma target to be proved from the same
  hypotheses, or as a paper-gap report; it must not become a bundled hypothesis
  consumed by downstream code.  Do not recommend adding a conditional helper
  merely to make a blueprint link pass.  An existing conditional helper may
  remain only as temporary quarantine for already useful proof content, with an
  explicit discharge or deletion plan, and it must stay off the paper theorem's
  `\leanok` path.
- **Conclusion.** Does the blueprint conclusion match the Lean return
  type? Watch for "$X$" vs "$X^\dagger$", "$=$" vs "$\leq$", strict
  vs non-strict inequalities, and conjugate-linear vs linear conventions
  (e.g. `mpvOverlap A B N = star (mpvInner A B N)` — the project's own
  `Fact-Check Lessons` in `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` calls this out).
- **Indexing conventions.** Blueprint indices run 0 to d−1 (matching
  `Fin d`). Flag if the blueprint silently uses 1 to d.
- **Definitions vs theorems.** If the blueprint asserts a fact ("X is a
  subalgebra"), it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not
  `\begin{definition}`.
- **Notation drift.** Does the blueprint use the established notation
  from `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` §"Notation Consistency"? Ad-hoc
  notation that disagrees with the Lean object is a sync bug.

For each mismatch, cite both the blueprint line and the Lean line, and
describe the mathematical discrepancy precisely. Do NOT accept "close
enough" — sync means equivalence, not similarity.

## Code review

**F1:** The paper constructs the global measurement through `lem:qld-4-7` at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`, then states `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` at lines 1463-1480 without a supplied `GlobalPairWitness` hypothesis. The new conditional helpers correctly expose that hypothesis and carry `**Unfaithful:**` markers, but those markers claim that `exists_pulled_apart_consistency` is stated in `Extraction.Construction`. Neither declaration nor module exists. The same nonexistent target is cited at `SuppliedPointConsistency.lean:104` and line 224.

Project policy permits this conditional scaffolding only when a real source-facing construction theorem or proof-obligation target remains visible. Add that theorem, with a tracked proof obligation for composing `exists_globalPairWitness` and handling its zero-error case, or cite an actual equivalent target. The paper-facing theorem must not inherit the witness premise.

**F2:** `scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve` reports `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis-given-global-pair` as `UNRESOLVED`. The existing source node is `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:220-284`. Either add an explicit formalization-only supplied-witness node or correct the citations without presenting the conditional theorem as the source lemma.

**F3:** The gap register says the proof of `lem:qld-unitary-given-global-pair` is open, but this PR proves `exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness` and adds `\leanok` at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:569-620`. Update the entry while retaining the accurate statement that source-level witness composition and range-projection transfer remain open.

The completed extraction proof itself is coherent: its small-error and large-error branches type-check, and the source `lem:qld-unitary` remains separately marked `\notready`. `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean` and `git diff --check` both pass; no unmarked proof hole was found in the completed dependency chain.

## Prose review

The category-A equivalence mismatches F2 and F3 are the most serious issues.

**F1/F4.** The cited `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis-given-global-pair` has no blueprint node, and repository search finds no `Extraction.Construction` containing the claimed source obligation. Add a separate formalization-only node that explicitly states the `GlobalPairWitness` hypothesis and links `tildeObs_selfConsistent_ofGlobalPairWitness`. Keep it separate from the source theorem’s `\leanok` path. The unfaithful marker must also point to an actual source-faithful construction theorem or named obligation.

**F2.** The blueprint places both conclusions after “For every unit vector,” but [`idealExpState_extractionAux0`](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-523-proof-exists-extractionwitness-ofglobalpairwitness/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EPRState.lean:128) has no normalization hypothesis; only [`exists_unit_aux_near_eprProjection`](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-523-proof-exists-extractionwitness-ofglobalpairwitness/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EPRState.lean:148) requires one. State the projection identity for arbitrary `\vartheta`, then impose unit norm for the existence conclusion.

**F3.** The blueprint defines `\Delta=\mathrm{aux}\otimes\mathrm{EPR}` before its “more generally” clause. By contrast, [`pauli_overlap_transfer`](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-523-proof-exists-extractionwitness-ofglobalpairwitness/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/OverlapTransfer.lean:126) quantifies independently over arbitrary normalized `theta` and `ideal`. Introduce an arbitrary normalized comparison state in the general statement, then specialize it to `\Delta` for the Pauli-distance theorem.

**F5.** The source statement of `lem:qld-unitary` is complete and its formalization status is already represented by the absence of `\leanok`. Remove `\notready`; that tag means the blueprint entry itself still needs clarification.

**F6.** Schwartz–Zippel is not needed to state the Pauli comparison, but it is used in the linked proofs. Move `lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree` from statement `\uses` to a proof-level `\uses` and record the other actual mathematical dependencies of the linked proofs there.

**F7.** Replace “re-exports the marginal and point consistency declarations” with “provides the marginal and point-consistency estimates,” or drop the sentence.

**F8–F11.** Drop “recovered from PR533 and PR539,” “preserved from PR #539, head …,” and the commit lists. Retain the paper, blueprint, and paper-gap citations and describe the relevant point-consistency, convolution, or collision estimates mathematically.

**F12.** Drop both occurrences of “This conditional proof has no `sorry` dependency.” The surrounding prose already explains the mathematical dependencies.

**F13.** Replace the blueprint phrase with “there exists a conditional extraction witness whenever `\delta\geq4`.” Make the corresponding change to “Construct every extraction-witness field” in `Unitary.lean:78`.

**F14.** Replace “remain open in Lean” and “proof debt” with a direct comparison of hypotheses: “This statement assumes the global measurement and therefore does not assert its construction or the unconditional extraction conclusion.”

Summary: 2 equivalence mismatches, 1 missing source-faithful target, 1 unresolved blueprint counterpart, 1 incorrect `\notready`, 1 dependency-annotation error, and 8 prose issues.

  1877	\end{proof}

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.

    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   123	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   124	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   125	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   126	argument.
   127	
   128	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   129	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   130	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   131	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   132	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness} concludes the
   133	existence of this data at the explicit extraction scale, but it takes the
   134	\path{GlobalPairWitness} of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7} as an explicit hypothesis
   135	rather than obtaining it from \path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  That bundle
   136	carries the projective global polynomial-pair measurements and both
   137	point-consistency estimates, and the blueprint proof of
   138	Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} obtains it from Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7}; deleting
   139	the hypothesis would leave that construction unproved.  By the criterion of
   140	\path{docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex} the hypothesis is therefore proof
   141	debt rather than a faithful boundary condition, and the declaration is a
   142	conditional helper: it does not certify the source lemma, and the blueprint
   143	node Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} accordingly neither links it nor carries any
   144	statement-level formalization mark.  The declaration is recorded instead on the
   145	separate formalization-support node
   146	\path{lem:qld-unitary-given-global-pair}, whose statement assumes the global
   147	polynomial-pair measurement explicitly and whose formal link points only to the
   148	conditional helper.  It therefore cannot be mistaken for the source result.
   149	Apart from that hypothesis the
   150	conclusion matches the Stage~4.2 extraction lemma, including the corrected
   151	numerical estimates; the later passage to the isometries in the soundness
   152	theorem is not formalized, and no declaration yet states that passage.
   153	
   154	The conditional character of the result is visible wherever the declaration is
   155	invoked: the suffix \path{ofGlobalPairWitness} names the extra premise in the
   156	declaration itself, and its docstring records the statement as conditional and
   157	its dependence on the assumed witness as unfaithful.  Discharging the debt
   158	requires composing \path{exists_globalPairWitness} with this helper to obtain
   159	the source lemma; no declaration carries out that composition.
   160	
   161	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   162	\ghissue{123} owns the source-facing composition through
   163	\path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  \ghissue{47} tracks the separate
   164	range-projection transfer needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must
   165	be derived from the concrete data rather than stored in the witness.
   166	
   167	\section{Conclusion}
   168	
   169	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   170	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   171	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   172	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   173	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   174	already supplied by the extraction lemma.  Independently of both defects, the
   175	present extraction declaration is conditional on the global polynomial-pair
   176	measurement, and that conditionality must be removed before it may be
   177	advertised as the source lemma.

     1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
